title: Groups 1, 7 and 0
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: How do you predict which metal will react more strongly?
Can you show me an example of a displacement reaction?
What does the group number tell us about reactivity?

explain.say: Today we will look at how elements react in groups.
Group one elements are very reactive metals.
Reactivity generally increases down Group one.
Group seventeen elements are the halogens.
Displacement reactions show which element is more reactive.
In everyday life, we see this with cleaning solutions.

faq.q: Why are the noble gases in Group 18 not very reactive?
faq.a: They have a full outer electron shell. This makes them very stable and unreactive.

faq.q: Does reactivity always increase down a group?
faq.a: No, reactivity trends differ between groups. For example, halogens decrease in reactivity down the group.
asks: Is there a general rule for reactivity trends?
Does the trend change for Group 17?

faq.q: What does a displacement reaction actually show?
faq.a: It shows that the element on the left is more reactive than the element on the right.
asks: How do I know which element is more reactive?
Is it just about the metal reacting?

faq.q: Do Group 1 metals always react with water?
faq.a: Yes, most Group 1 metals react vigorously with water, releasing hydrogen gas.
asks: What happens when Group 1 metals meet water?

faq.q: Can I predict the reaction between two unknown elements?
faq.a: You can predict it by comparing their positions on the reactivity series or group trends.
asks: How do I predict a reaction?
Do I need a chart to predict reactions?

facts: Group one elements are known as the alkali metals.
Reactivity generally increases down Group one elements.
Halogens in Group 17 become less reactive as you go down the group.
In a displacement reaction, the more reactive element displaces the less reactive one.

quiz.say: Which element is most reactive in Group one?
quiz.why: Potassium is the largest element in Group one, and reactivity increases down this group.

wrong.0: Lithium is at the top of the group, so its reactivity is much lower.
wrong.1: Sodium is more reactive than lithium, but potassium is even more reactive.
wrong.2: Calcium is in Group 2, not Group 1, so it does not follow this trend.

quiz.say: If element A displaces element B, what must be true?

options.show: A is more reactive than B
options.say: A is more reactive than B

options.show: B is more reactive than A
options.say: B is more reactive than A

quiz.why: For displacement to happen, the element doing the displacing must be more reactive.

wrong.0: If they were equal, no reaction or displacement would occur.
wrong.1: While temperature matters, the primary factor shown by displacement is relative reactivity.
wrong.3: If B were more reactive, it would displace A instead.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes Group 17 reactivity?

options.show: Reactivity depends only on the period
options.say: Reactivity depends only on the period

quiz.why: As you go down Group 17, the attraction for electrons decreases, lowering reactivity.

wrong.1: This is incorrect because the outer electrons are further from the nucleus.
wrong.2: The size of the atoms changes, which affects their chemical properties.
wrong.3: Reactivity is primarily determined by the group number and position.
